rationale: The available literature does not support the hypothesis that bifid uvula (HP:0000193) is present in at least 40% of evaluated individuals with SMAD2-mediated Loeys-Dietz syndrome (LDS6), nor that it acts as a sensitive discriminator. Multiple specialized LDS cohorts (Jani et al. 2020, Koefoed et al. 2025) report an absence of SMAD2 patients or note that SMAD2 pathogenic variants remain exceptionally scarce (only 9 reported up to Camerota et al. 2019). Furthermore, where craniofacial phenotypes are systematically characterized across LDS subtypes, bifid uvula is predominantly restricted to TGFBR1 (LDS1) and TGFBR2 (LDS2), being absent or rare in downstream pathway components, and overall palate abnormalities are observed far less frequently than originally described.

evidence.text: In a comprehensive genotype-phenotype assessment of LDS, abnormal palate and bifid uvula were not as frequently found as historically described across non-receptor subtypes, and only 9 (likely) pathogenic variants in SMAD2 had been reported in the literature.

source.quote: Most typically, LDS patients present with aortic aneurysms and arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism, and bifid/broad uvula or cleft palate.

conflicts: Textbook descriptions continue to list bifid uvula as a core diagnostic criterion across all Loeys-Dietz syndrome types, whereas subtyping studies reveal that bifid uvula is predominantly enriched in TGFBR1/TGFBR2 cases and is infrequently reported in SMAD2/3 or TGFB2/3 cohorts.
The 40% threshold for bifid uvula in SMAD2 cannot be empirically sustained due to the extreme scarcity of published SMAD2 clinical cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance of palatal abnormalities (cleft palate, submucous cleft, and bifid uvula) across pooled, verified international registries of heterozygous SMAD2 pathogenic variant carriers?
new_directions.rationale: SMAD2 cohorts in single institutions are underpowered (often 0 patients). An international multi-center registry analysis is required to obtain precise numerators and denominators for craniofacial traits.

new_directions.question_text: Does SMAD2 missense versus truncating or MH2 domain variation result in distinct vascular and craniofacial penetrance profiles?
